newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani Islamist group plans 'corruption courts'.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani Islamist group plans 'corruption courts'.

text.p: The youth wing of a fundamentalist Islamist party said on Monday it would set up its own courts to try corrupt politicians in Pakistan and stop them from contesting general elections set for February 3.

The official APP news agency quoted Shabab-i-Milli secretary-general Suleman Butt as saying in the Punjab province capital of Lahore that the group's planned "accountability courts" comprising retired judges or senior lawyers would be set up in all major cities and would start functioning from January 8.
However, the trials will be symbolic and those accused will be tried in absentia.

Butt said that while the proposed courts would not exercise judicial powers, they would create an awareness among the general public of what he called the fraudulent activities of corrupt politicians and bureaucrats.

Shabab-i-Milli is the youth wing of the Jamaat-i-Islami party, which said on Sunday it would boycott the elections because the caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid's government had failed to call corrupt politicians into account as promised.

Jamaat chief Qazi Hussain Ahmad said on Sunday the elections would bring back the same corrupt elements who dominated the federal parliament and provincial assemblies in the past if they were not stopped from contesting the February elections.
Shabab-e-Milli has asked people to bring alleged cases of corruption and embezzlement of public funds to its notice.

The latest elections follow President Farooq Leghari's dismissal of prime minister Benazir Bhutto's government on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule. The National Assembly (lower house of parliament) and the four provincial assemblies were also dissolved.
Allegations of corruption by parliamentarians and bureaucrats has become a major issue for the coming elections in Pakistan, where four elected governments have been sacked over the past eight years.
